question.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=(y-x)\,i$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=({t}^{2}-t)\,i+({t}^{3}-t)\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,1).$
question.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{2}-t,\,y={t}^{3}-t,\,z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(y-x)\,i \\  & =({t}^{3}-t-{t}^{2}+t)\,i \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\,)\,k \\  & =(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\,({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,i\,)\cdot (\,(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)\,k\,) \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\cdot (2t-1)+0\cdot (3{t}^{2}-1)+0\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t) \\  & =2{t}^{4}-{t}^{3}-2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2} \\  & =2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\,2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}\,)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{2{t}^{5}}{5}-\frac{3{t}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{3})-(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{60}\end{aligned}
$$
